title: XMRig_Cryptominer_Investigation_226
description: Investigate unusual CPU usage on Linux servers potentially caused by cryptocurrency mining activity.
outcomes: Analysis of system services and processes

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The organization has detected unusual CPU usage on several Linux servers. Initial analysis suggests potential cryptocurrency mining activity. Your task is to investigate and contain this threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the miner-host system with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From this system, you can investigate the local host and potentially other connected systems. Enter `start` to begin.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the miner-host system with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From this system, you can investigate the local host and potentially other connected systems. Enter `start` to begin.

levels.title: Investigate Unusual CPU Usage
levels.content: Investigate the unusual CPU usage on the miner-host system by checking running services and processes. Identify the service responsible for the abnormal CPU utilization.
levels.solution: Check running services and processes to identify any unusual or unauthorized activity. The service responsible for the abnormal CPU utilization is `sys-monitor`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check running services and processes to identify any unusual or unauthorized activity.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for any services or processes that are consuming an unusually high amount of CPU resources.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `ps aux | grep -i 'sys-monitor'` to check for the suspicious service.

levels.title: Determine Network Communication
levels.content: Investigate the network communication associated with the suspicious service by examining network connections. Identify the external IP address the suspicious service is communicating with.
levels.solution: Examine network connections and analyze traffic patterns to identify suspicious communication. The external IP address the suspicious service is communicating with is `185.183.98.46`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine network connections using tools like `netstat` or `ss` to identify suspicious communication.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for any connections to external IP addresses that are not part of the organization's network.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `netstat -tuln | grep -i '185.183.98.46'` to check for suspicious network connections.

levels.title: Investigate Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Investigate how the malicious service maintains persistence on the system by checking system service configurations. Identify the system service used to ensure the malicious software runs automatically after a reboot.
levels.solution: Check system service configurations and look for any unauthorized or suspicious services. The system service used to ensure the malicious software runs automatically after a reboot is `sys-monitor`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check system service configurations using `systemctl` or `service` commands to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for any services that are set to start automatically at boot and are related to the suspicious activity.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service | grep -i 'sys-monitor'` to check for suspicious services.
